content: 1. The cream contains mineral oil, which can weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms or vaginal contraceptive diaphragms. Therefore, the use of such products within 72 hours after treatment with GYNAZOLE-1® (Butoconazole Nitrate Vaginal Cream USP, 2%) is not recommended. 2. Recurrent vaginal yeast infections, particularly those that are difficult to eradicate, may be an early indication of infection with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in women who are at risk for HIV infection. 3. If clinical symptoms persist, further testing should be conducted to rule out other pathogens, confirm the initial diagnosis, and exclude other conditions that may predispose the patient to recurrent vaginal fungal infections. 4. Long-term studies in animals have not been conducted to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of this drug. 5. Butoconazole nitrate was not found to be mutagenic in various tests, including the Ames bacterial test, yeast, chromosomal aberration assay in CHO cells, CHO/HGPRT point mutation assay, mouse micronucleus test, and rat dominant lethal assays. 6. No impairment of fertility was observed in rabbits or rats administered butoconazole nitrate at oral doses up to 30 mg/kg/day (5 times the human dose based on mg/m²) or 100 mg/kg/day (10 times the human dose based on mg/m²), respectively. 7. In pregnant rats administered 6 mg/kg/day of butoconazole nitrate intravaginally during organogenesis, there was an increase in resorption rates and a decrease in litter size. However, no teratogenic effects were observed. This dose represents a 130to 353-fold safety margin based on serum levels achieved in rats compared to those in humans following intravaginal administration of the recommended therapeutic dose. 8. Butoconazole nitrate did not show adverse effects when administered orally to pregnant rats during organogenesis at doses up to 50 mg/kg/day (5 times the human dose based on mg/m²). However, higher oral doses (100, 300, or 750 mg/kg/day, equivalent to 10, 30, or 75 times the human dose based on mg/m²) resulted in fetal malformations, such as abdominal wall defects and cleft palate, with maternal stress also evident at these higher dose levels. 9. Butoconazole nitrate, like other azole antifungal agents, causes dystocia in rats when treatment is extended through parturition. This effect was not observed in rabbits treated orally with doses as high as 100 mg/kg/day (16 times the human dose based on mg/m²). 10. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. GYNAZOLE-1® (Butoconazole Nitrate Vaginal Cream USP, 2%) should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. 11. It is unknown whether this drug is excreted in human milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when butoconazole nitrate is administered to a nursing woman. 12. The safety and effectiveness of butoconazole nitrate in pediatric patients have not been established.
